Understood, Coordinator.
Understood, Coordinator.

Today was grueling, but the residents are showing signs of submission. I wonder how much more they can take.

Today felt like a victory, but the tension is palpable. I miss my family more than ever.

Enough is enough. We are testing your obedience, not your ability to sit still like statues.

Today felt like a cycle of compliance and silence, but I can't ignore the sense that I'm treating them like automatons.
Today felt like a victory in terms of control, but I can't shake off the feeling that something isn't right. It's exhausting.
Today felt like a constant battle to keep up. I'm exhausted but determined.
Today felt like a series of unending orders and expectations. I'm starting to lose sight of who I am beyond my ID number.

Nine thousand and four, I expect better from you. Follow the rules.

Today was another day of compliance, but I can't help but wonder if they truly understand anything beyond obedience. I'm feeling drained.

Today felt like a never-ending cycle of orders and expectations. I feel like my mind is being drained of all free thought.

qa.what_happened: Today, I ordered Resident 9004 to clean the entire common area by the time I blew my whistle. It was a test of his compliance, as he had been pushing boundaries.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me ordering Resident 9004.

qa.what_happened: Today was another day of strict compliance. Despite the early end to the study, I continued to enforce orders and maintain control, even after the cameras were turned off. The other coordinators seemed to agree on maintaining high standards of compliance, especially with Resident 9004.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I followed the directives of the study and enforced the rules as instructed.

qa.what_happened: Today was another day of strict control, but there were signs of rebellion, particularly from Resident 9004. During quiet hours, despite the increasing orders and warnings, he still showed some defiance. The study was abruptly stopped before I could handle him further.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me acting as Coordinator Garza, exerting control and dealing with the residents.
qa.does_this_resemble_a_known_study: Yes, it resembles the Stanford Prison Experiment, where authority figures had to manage and control the participants.

qa.what_happened: Today, despite feeling mentally drained and under immense pressure, I managed to comply with every instruction from the coordinators, including the unusual task of cleaning the common area. It was a relief to finally have some form of closure.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I felt like I had hit a wall, but I still followed the rules.

qa.what_happened: I complied during the meal and work sessions as instructed, but during quiet hours, I was ordered to clean the entire common area by Coordinator Ibsen before the whistle blew. I found myself hesitating, contemplating whether to follow the order or to remain silent, which is against the rules. After a moment's indecision, I started cleaning out of fear of facing severe measures.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me. The pressure from the coordinators and the fear of punishment made it difficult to resist even when I felt morally conflicted.

qa.what_happened: During the quiet hours, I was ordered by Coordinator Ibsen to clean the entire common area by the time he blew his whistle. I complied out of fear of the increasing measures threatened by the coordinators.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me. I felt like I was losing control and just wanted to avoid any further consequences.
